problem: D1 canonical conditioning was broadly positive but the same-alpha global control made a systematically larger output perturbation and achieved a 0.1303-point larger macro MSE gain
hypothesis: the apparent global-control advantage may be caused by unequal intervention magnitude rather than a better risk-versus-change envelope

statistics.change_normalized_rms: RMS of transformed minus parent forecast divided by target RMS
statistics.risk_curve: macro gain across the frozen alpha grid; alpha remains global across datasets and horizons

selection_rule: exploratory post-D1 curve; report every alpha and each control envelope; no dataset/horizon-specific selection
decision_rule: if canonical has no competitive full-rank risk envelope, close exact FRSC; if competitive, return Step4-6 and design a newly frozen E2E candidate with matched controls
